per_column.name: writing_quality_issue
per_column.rationale: Directly addresses the query on why audiences are dissatisfied by categorizing writing-related complaints, giving a genuine grouping axis. Values are well-grounded: IMDB-0001 mentions 'stilted dialogue' (poor_dialogue) and 'insipid/uninspired' writing; IMDB-0003 'wooden performances' maps loosely to uninspired_writing. not_present used appropriately for silent rows. Minor slippage where multiple issues co-exist but single value chosen, but no invented facts.

per_column.name: plot_structural_issue
per_column.rationale: Provides a distinct plot/structure axis complementary to writing, useful for explaining dissatisfaction. IMDB-0003's 'predictable and well-trodden premise' soundly supports predictable_plot. not_present correctly assigned to positive reviews and rows without plot complaints. Categorizations are warranted readings; no evident fabrication.

per_column.name: genre_execution_quality
per_column.rationale: Combining genre with failure verdict gives a useful axis to compare dissatisfaction across genres. Grounding is mostly sound: IMDB-0002 explicitly about a horror movie (failed_horror), IMDB-0003 discusses 'drama' (failed_drama). However IMDB-0001 (Stargate SG-1, sci-fi) labeled 'failed_drama' is a weak/questionable genre inference, and 'failed_' framing risks conflating negative label with genre where text may not explicitly deem the genre failed. Positive reviews correctly not_present.

judge.rationale: All three added columns give genuine, distinct analytical axes (writing, plot, genre execution) directly relevant to 'why IMDb audiences are dissatisfied,' enabling grouping and comparison beyond the raw label_pos flag. Values are generally sound readings of the source text with appropriate not_present handling for silent/positive rows. The main weakness is occasional over-confident genre categorization (e.g., a sci-fi TV show tagged failed_drama), which slightly lowers groundedness, but no gross fabrications are observed.
